mechanism_narrative: A 2% quarterly increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strengthening economic growth, leading to increased consumer spending and, subsequently, higher S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in > 55% of instances following a 2%+ GDPC1 increase, over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) signals accommodative monetary policy, supporting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward SPX returns during periods of FEDFUNDS < 0.5% are not significantly higher than those during periods of FEDFUNDS > 1% (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 5%, indicating a tight labor market, S&P 500 returns tend to be positive over the next 60 trading days due to increased consumer confidence and spending.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in > 50% of instances when UNRATE is below 5%, over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) coupled with a decrease in housing starts (HOUST) signals a shift towards more productive investments, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (INDPRO > 1% and HOUST < -2%) fails to predict positive SPX returns in > 60% of instances, over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in retail sales (RSAFS) above 5% YoY indicates strong consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in > 55% of instances following a 5%+ RSAFS YoY increase, over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The difference between FEDFUNDS and the 10-year Treasury yield (not directly observable, using FEDFUNDS as a proxy for the yield spread) being above 1% signals a steepening yield curve, typically associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The implied yield spread (using FEDFUNDS as a proxy) fails to predict positive SPX returns in > 60% of instances, over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 jobs in a month, indicating strong labor market growth, S&P 500 returns tend to be positive over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in > 50% of instances following a PAYEMS increase of > 200,000, over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% MoM, indicating easing inflation pressures, tends to lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as real incomes rise.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in > 55% of instances following a 0.5%+ CPIAUCSL MoM decrease, over any 3-year rolling window.
